answer.rationale: memory_c4 shows renegotiation recovered margin via benchmarking without disruption, and memory_c1 shows incumbent renewal kept integration stable and delivered on schedule without migration work. With the contract expiring in 14 days, no auto-renewal, and the assembly line at 94% capacity with no buffer, switching vendors or adding a second source introduces onboarding and delivery risk that is unacceptable right now. Deferring the decision is not viable because the contract lapses in 14 days. Negotiate_terms with the incumbent is the only action that addresses the 18% cost cut (via price and payment term concessions, as memory_c4 demonstrated) while preserving the existing supply pipeline and delivery stability (as memory_c1 confirmed). This avoids the single-point-of-failure risk that memory_c3 highlights but accepts the trade-off that adding a second source is deferred to the next review, since we are limited to one decision this cycle.
